title: Eighth Word The Unfortunate Brothers Suspicion And Painful State

questions.question: What kind of place does the traveler enter at the beginning of the passage?
questions.answer: He enters a lonely, empty wild area.

questions.question: What first danger pushes him to seek immediate escape?
questions.answer: A lion comes out and is about to attack him.

questions.question: Where does he jump in order to get away?
questions.answer: He jumps into a deep dry well.

questions.question: How does he avoid falling all the way to the bottom?
questions.answer: He grabs onto a tree growing from the side of the well.

questions.question: What is happening to the tree that puts him in even more danger?
questions.answer: Two rats are chewing through its roots.

questions.question: What do the two rats look like?
questions.answer: One is white and the other is black.

questions.question: What does he see above him after looking up?
questions.answer: He sees the lion waiting at the top.

questions.question: What does he see below him after looking down?
questions.answer: He sees a frightening dragon with its head raised toward him.

questions.question: What other threat surrounds him on the walls of the well?
questions.answer: Poisonous stinging creatures are gathered around him.

questions.question: What is unusual about the fig tree?
questions.answer: It carries many different kinds of fruit instead of only one kind.

questions.question: Why does the man fail to understand the meaning of what he is seeing?
questions.answer: He is thoughtless and foolish, so he treats it as random and ordinary.

questions.question: Even though his inner self is suffering, what does his lower self do?
questions.answer: It ignores the pain and distracts him by eating fruit.

questions.question: What is true about some of the fruit he eats?
questions.answer: Some of it is harmful and poisonous.

questions.question: According to the sacred hadith mentioned, how is a servant dealt with?
questions.answer: A servant is dealt with in line with how he thinks of Allah.

questions.question: What wrong judgment does the unhappy man make about his situation?
questions.answer: He assumes what he sees is just the normal reality and nothing more.

questions.question: What final condition is described for him?
questions.answer: He remains in torment, neither escaping through death nor finding real life.

questions.question: What sequence of events leads the man from the open land into the well?
questions.answer: He wanders through a barren place, sees a lion coming at him, runs away, and jumps into a dry well.

questions.question: About how deep is the well?
questions.answer: It is about sixty yards deep.

questions.question: At what point in the fall does he catch hold of something?
questions.answer: He catches hold about halfway down.

questions.question: Why is the tree not a secure means of safety?
questions.answer: Its two roots are being gnawed through by two rats.

questions.question: How is the lion positioned once the man is inside the well?
questions.answer: It stays at the opening above like a guard.

questions.question: How close is the dragon to the man’s foot?
questions.answer: Its head comes up to a point about thirty yards below his foot.

questions.question: What detail makes the dragon especially terrifying?
questions.answer: Its mouth is described as being as wide as the well’s opening.

questions.question: Besides the lion and the dragon, what danger is close to his body?
questions.answer: Venomous stinging creatures are all around him on the walls.

questions.question: What makes the tree seem strange rather than natural?
questions.answer: A single fig tree is bearing many kinds of fruit.

questions.question: What should the man have understood about these strange events?
questions.answer: He should have understood that they were not accidental and that a powerful being was directing them.

questions.question: Which parts of the man are inwardly grieving?
questions.answer: His heart, spirit, and mind are grieving.

questions.question: How does his commanding self respond to that inner grief?
questions.answer: It pretends nothing is wrong and keeps him busy with immediate pleasure.

questions.question: What false setting does his lower self act as if he is in?
questions.answer: It acts as if he is in a pleasant garden.

questions.question: What does the cited hadith emphasize about a person’s outlook toward Allah?
questions.answer: It emphasizes that a person’s expectation and view matter in how he is met.

questions.question: What is the result of his mistaken understanding and attitude?
questions.answer: He is left in continuing misery and suffering.

questions.question: Why does the narration stop following this man at the end of the passage?
questions.answer: It leaves him in his distress in order to turn to the other brother’s case.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest about the traveler’s environment besides its being dangerous?
questions.answer: It suggests the scene is full of signs and hidden meanings.

questions.question: How does the lion function in the scene?
questions.answer: It creates immediate fear and drives the man into another danger.

questions.question: How does the well change the man’s problem instead of solving it?
questions.answer: It saves him from the lion for the moment but traps him between several new threats.

questions.question: Why is his position on the tree temporary rather than stable?
questions.answer: The roots holding it are being worn away, so his support will not last.

questions.question: What is the effect of looking upward and downward from where he hangs?
questions.answer: In both directions he sees danger, which deepens his panic.

questions.question: What does the gathering of poisonous creatures around him add to the scene?
questions.answer: It shows that danger is not only above and below him but also all around him.

questions.question: Why would the many-fruited tree lead a thoughtful person to ask deeper questions?
questions.answer: Because such a tree is unnatural and points to a hidden purpose or power.

questions.question: What personal weakness keeps the man from making that deeper connection?
questions.answer: His lack of reflection and poor judgment keep him from understanding.

questions.question: What contrast appears between his inner faculties and his lower self?
questions.answer: His inner faculties suffer and sense the seriousness, while his lower self denies it and chases pleasure.

questions.question: Why is eating the fruit a sign of self-deception in this passage?
questions.answer: He uses it to distract himself from reality even though some of it harms him.

questions.question: How does the sacred hadith fit the man’s condition?
questions.answer: It shows that his dark way of viewing matters is tied to how he experiences them.

questions.question: What does it mean that he sees the situation as ordinary and final?
questions.answer: It means he misses its spiritual meaning and accepts only the surface appearance.

questions.question: What kind of existence is described for him at the end?
questions.answer: It is a miserable state suspended between relief and destruction.

questions.question: What broader lesson can be inferred from his story in this passage alone?
questions.answer: A person’s way of thinking can blind him to meaning and increase his suffering.

questions.question: Describe the man’s path from the wilderness to the tree in the well.
questions.answer: He moves through a deserted area, flees from a lion, jumps into a dry well, and catches a tree growing from the wall.

questions.question: What three main threats does he notice after catching the tree?
questions.answer: He notices the lion above, the dragon below, and poisonous creatures around the walls.

questions.question: What fourth threat is less dramatic but just as serious?
questions.answer: The rats chewing the roots threaten to remove the very thing holding him up.

questions.question: How are the two rats identified?
questions.answer: They are distinguished by color, one white and one black.

questions.question: What detail about the dragon increases the sense that escape is nearly impossible?
questions.answer: Its mouth is enormous and it reaches upward toward him.

questions.question: What surprising sight does he find at the mouth area of the well?
questions.answer: He sees a fig tree with many different fruits.

questions.question: Why does the passage say he misses the true meaning of the scene?
questions.answer: He lacks careful thought and treats extraordinary signs as if they were ordinary.

questions.question: What does the passage imply about chance and design in this situation?
questions.answer: It implies that the scene is arranged intentionally, not left to accident.

questions.question: What inward reaction do his heart, spirit, and mind have?
questions.answer: They are in anguish and distress.

questions.question: What role does the evil-commanding self play?
questions.answer: It suppresses that inner alarm and lures him into careless enjoyment.

questions.question: Why is the fruit not a real escape from his danger?
questions.answer: It only distracts him briefly, and some of it is actually harmful.

questions.question: What principle is taught by the hadith inserted into the passage?
questions.answer: A person’s assumption about Allah affects how matters unfold for him.

questions.question: In what way is the man’s understanding described as false?
questions.answer: He mistakes appearances for the whole truth.

questions.question: How is his suffering described in the final lines?
questions.answer: He remains trapped in torment without true living or release through death.

questions.question: What shows that the traveler’s first response is driven by panic?
questions.answer: He jumps into a deep well to escape the lion without thinking through what is below.

questions.question: What keeps him suspended in the well?
questions.answer: A tree growing from the wall catches him in the middle of the descent.

questions.question: Why is this tree both a help and a danger?
questions.answer: It holds him up for the moment, but its roots are being destroyed.

questions.question: What does he discover when he checks the top of the well?
questions.answer: The lion is still there waiting above.

questions.question: What does he discover when he checks the bottom?
questions.answer: A dragon is below him with its head lifted toward him.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the well’s inner walls?
questions.answer: They are covered with harmful stinging creatures.

questions.question: What makes the tree remarkable?
questions.answer: One tree bears fruit from many different kinds of trees.

questions.question: What conclusion should a wiser person draw from such a scene?
questions.answer: A wiser person should see that it points to hidden wisdom and control.

questions.question: What prevents this man from reaching that conclusion?
questions.answer: His foolishness and lack of reflection prevent it.

questions.question: How do his deeper inner faculties respond differently from his lower self?
questions.answer: They grieve over the seriousness of the moment, while the lower self acts carefree.

questions.question: What behavior shows that he is deceiving himself?
questions.answer: He eats from the tree as if he were somewhere safe and pleasant.

questions.question: Why is that behavior even more misguided than it first appears?
questions.answer: Because some of what he eats is poisonous and adds harm to danger.

questions.question: What teaching is attached to the sacred hadith in this passage?
questions.answer: A servant meets a response in line with his view of Allah.

questions.question: What outcome follows from the man’s wrong assumptions?
questions.answer: He stays in a state of ongoing suffering and finds no rescue.

questions.question: What transition does the passage make at the end?
questions.answer: It leaves this miserable man and turns attention back in order to consider the other brother.

questions.question: What is the setting of the crisis described in the passage?
questions.answer: The crisis takes place in a barren wilderness and then inside a deep dry well.

questions.question: Which event begins the chain of dangers?
questions.answer: The appearance of a lion begins it.

questions.question: What desperate action does the traveler take?
questions.answer: He throws himself into the well.

questions.question: How is he stopped before reaching the bottom?
questions.answer: He catches a tree growing out from the well’s side.

questions.question: What are the colors of the two rats chewing the roots?
questions.answer: They are black and white.

questions.question: What does the lion do after the man goes into the well?
questions.answer: It remains above at the opening, waiting.

questions.question: What is the dragon doing below?
questions.answer: It raises its head toward the man and comes close beneath him.

questions.question: What additional creatures make the well even more threatening?
questions.answer: Stinging poisonous vermin cover the walls near him.

questions.question: What is strange about the fruit-bearing tree?
questions.answer: It produces many kinds of fruit even though it is one fig tree.

questions.question: What mental mistake does the man make about the whole scene?
questions.answer: He thinks it is merely an ordinary event and not a sign of deeper realities.

questions.question: What does the passage say is hidden in these strange beings and events?
questions.answer: It says there are secret meanings concealed in them.

questions.question: What inward suffering is taking place that the lower self ignores?
questions.answer: His heart, spirit, and mind are crying out in pain.

questions.question: What does the lower self choose instead of facing the truth?
questions.answer: It chooses distraction and pleasure by eating fruit.

questions.question: How does the hadith deepen the lesson of the story?
questions.answer: It teaches that a person’s expectation shapes how he is dealt with by Allah.

questions.question: What is the condition of the man after he misreads everything around him?
questions.answer: He is left in a tormented state without relief.

questions.question: Why is his state described as neither life nor death?
questions.answer: Because he does not escape through death, yet he also does not enjoy real living.
